arxiv-2108-01916.title: Free-free background radiation from accreting primordial black holes
arxiv-2108-01916.creator: Hiroyuki Tashiro, Katsuya T. Abe, Teppei Minoda
arxiv-2108-01916.description: Abstract Baryonic gas falling onto a primordial black hole (PBH) emits photons via the free-free process. These photons can contribute the diffuse free-free background radiation in the frequency range of the cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB). We show that the intensity of the free-free background radiation from PBHs depends on the mass and abundance of PBHs.

arxiv-2305-11947.title: Cesium atoms in cryogenic argon matrix
arxiv-2305-11947.creator: T. Battard (1), S. Lahs (1), C. Crépin (2), D. Comparat (1)
arxiv-2305-11947.description: Abstract This paper presents both experimental and theoretical investigations into the spectroscopy of dilute cesium (Cs) atoms within a solid argon (Ar) matrix at cryogenic temperatures. This system is relevant for matrix isolation spectroscopy and in particular for recently proposed methods for investigating phenomena that extend beyond the standard model of particle physics.

arxiv-2503-22457.title: The Rigid Unit Mode spectrum for symmetric frameworks
arxiv-2503-22457.creator: Eleftherios Kastis, Derek Kitson
arxiv-2503-22457.description: Abstract . We establish several fundamental properties of the Rigid Unit Mode (RUM) spectrum for symmetric frameworks with a discrete abelian symmetry group and arbitrary linear constraints. In particular, we identify a nonempty subset of the RUM spectrum which derives from the joint eigenvalues of generators for the linear part of the symmetry group.

pmc-10656506.title: Clinical subtypes in patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder
pmc-10656506.creator: Aline Seger, Anja Ophey, Christopher E. J. Doppler, Johanna Kickartz, Marie-Sophie Lindner, Maximilian Hommelsen, Gereon R. Fink, Michael Sommerauer
pmc-10656506.description: Patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) show a broad heterogeneity in clinical presentation, and subtypes may already arise in prodromal disease stages. Isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is the most specific marker of prodromal PD, but data on clinical subtyping of patients with iRBD remain scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to identify iRBD subtypes.

pmc-10736648.title: DOES HEARING LOSS MODERATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN COGNITION AND DEPRESSION?
pmc-10736648.creator: Jennifer Lister, Aryn Harrison Bush, Jennifer O’Brien, Laura Conover, Nasreen Sadeq
pmc-10736648.description: Hearing loss, depression, and cognitive impairment are common, co-occurring conditions experienced by older adults, but the nature of the relationship among these conditions remains unclear. Both depression and hearing loss have been identified as risk factors for dementia, but for different stages of life (e.g., Singh-Manoux et al., 2017; Livingston et al., 2020).

pmc-11493814.title: High-Fugacity Expansion and Crystallization in Non-sliding Hard-Core Lattice Particle Models Without a Tiling Constraint
pmc-11493814.creator: Qidong He, Ian Jauslin
pmc-11493814.description: In this paper, we prove the existence of a crystallization transition for a family of hard-core particle models on periodic graphs in dimension d≥2. We consider only models featuring a single species of particles, which in particular forbids the particles from rotation and reflection, and establish a criterion under which crystallization occurs at sufficiently high densities.

pmc-11644658.title: Geographical Distribution Dynamics of Acorus calamus in China Under Climate Change
pmc-11644658.creator: Chunlei Yue, Hepeng Li, Xiaodeng Shi, Sanja Manitašević Jovanović, Ana Vuleta, Yuval Sapir
pmc-11644658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Acorus calamus, a perennial emergent herb, is highly valued for its ornamental appeal, water purification ability, and medicinal properties. However, there is a significant contradiction between the rapidly increasing demand for A. calamus and the diminishing wild resources. Understanding its geographical distribution and the influence of global climate change on its geographical distribution is imperative for establishing a theoretical framework for the conservation of natural resources and the expansion of its cultivation. In this study, 266 distribution records of A.

pmc-11653636.title: Factors affecting survival of foals with pneumonia in a referral hospital
pmc-11653636.creator: Heini Sofia Rossi, Heli Katariina Hyytiäinen, Jouni Juho Tapio Junnila, Minna Marjaana Rajamäki, Anna Kristina Mykkänen
pmc-11653636.description: BackgroundPneumonia is a common condition in ailing neonatal foals, and it remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in this veterinary patient group. Factors affecting the survival of young foals with pneumonia have not been thoroughly investigated. The aim of this study was to explore the potential prognostic factors associated with survival of these foals.

pmc-11656550.title: Aromatase inhibitors for short stature in male children and adolescents treated with growth hormone: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-11656550.creator: Kan Wang, Fei Ye, Da-Yan Wang, Pan-Jian Lai, Lin-Qian Zhang
pmc-11656550.description: Whether the addition of aromatase inhibitors (AIs) to recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) could yield additional benefit for short stature is controversial. We aimed to assess the effects of combined AIs and rhGH versus those of rhGH alone for short stature using a meta-analytic approach.

pmc-11716715.title: Social Deprivation and Cognition in Older Adulthood: The Mediating Role of Lifestyle Activities
pmc-11716715.creator: Lena M Hofbauer, Francisca S Rodriguez
pmc-11716715.description: BackgroundPrevious research has shown that the experience of social deprivation is associated with impaired cognition in older adulthood. It has been proposed that this may be explained by social deprivation being associated with a less ‘brain‐healthy’ lifestyle. We thus investigate mediating effects of lifestyle in the association between social deprivation and cognition.MethodsData of 3,015 respondents (Mean Age: 74.

pmc-12528610.title: Factors influencing fenestration and dehiscence in the anterior teeth after clear aligner treatment: a multicenter retrospective study
pmc-12528610.creator: Zhixin Song, Qian Liu, Houzhuo Luo, Xinyue Fan, Mingxin Zhang, Baoning Liu, Bin Yan, Xiaodong Zhang, Liling Ren, Yanning Ma, Zuolin Jin
pmc-12528610.description: ObjectiveThis retrospective clinical study, using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), examined the presence of fenestration and dehiscence in anterior teeth following non-extraction clear aligner therapy, along with the associated risk factors.MethodsThe study included 224 adult patients who underwent non-extraction clear aligner treatment. CBCT scans taken before (T1) and after treatment (T2) were analyzed to detect the presence of fenestration and dehiscence.

pmc-12602255.title: Evidence‐Based Behavioral Interventions to Improve the Double‐Duty Actions Impacting the Dual Burden of Malnutrition: A Scoping Review
pmc-12602255.creator: Mary O Hearst, Elizabeth Weinfurter, Lillian Norman, Clara A Normile, Hussen Mekonnen, Melissa N Laska
pmc-12602255.description: There are three double‐duty actions that prevent both stunting and obesity, the dual burden of malnutrition, that can be implemented at health clinics worldwide. They are breastfeeding, young child nutrition, and antenatal care and women's nutrition. There is no scoping review that provides a summary of evidence‐based interventions that increase the double‐duty actions.

pmc-12610469.title: A Dynamic Pose-Testing Technique of Landing Gear Combined Stereo Vision and CAD Digital Model
pmc-12610469.creator: Wendong Zhang, Xianmin Chen, Baoquan Shi, Yao Li
pmc-12610469.description: The landing gear is one of the key components of an aircraft, enduring significant forces during takeoff and landing, and is influenced by various uncertain factors related to its structure. Therefore, conducting strength tests on the landing gear structure to study its ultimate load capacity is of great significance for structural design and analysis.

pmc-12646260.title: Appendiceal endometrioma mimicking appendiceal neoplasm
pmc-12646260.creator: Jason Douglas Cox, Agnes P Benjamin, John Ciciulla, Chun Hin Angus Lee
pmc-12646260.description: Endometriosis of the vermiform appendix is an uncommon pathology that may present as an appendiceal mass identified on colonoscopy. This may be due to an appendiceal endometrioma or intussusception of the appendix. Mucinous appendiceal neoplasms and neuroendocrine tumors are important clinical differentials. When there is concern for possible malignancy, resection is recommended, usually as a stapled cecectomy.

pmc-12698652.title: Effects of deep tillage combined with organic amendments application on carbon and nitrogen storage within aggregates and wheat yield
pmc-12698652.creator: Wenlong Cheng, Rongyan Bu, Shang Han, Shan Tang, Hui Wang, Min Li, Rui Zhu, Fahui Jiang, Mengmeng Tang, Ji Wu
pmc-12698652.description: IntroductionSoil organic carbon (SOC) and total nitrogen (TN) stocks are key determinants of the productive capacity of agricultural soils. This study aims to elucidate the effects of long-term tillage practices combined with organic amendments on SOC and TN sequestration within soil aggregates and their subsequent relationship with wheat yield.

pmc-13119509.title: Effect of Extremely Low-Frequency Pulsed Electromagnetic Field Intensity and Exposure Time on Pseudomonas aeruginosa: An In Vitro Study
pmc-13119509.creator: Amal M. El Sawy, Fahda N. Algahtani, Reem Barakat, Aly F. Mohamed, Yosef T. Aladadi
pmc-13119509.description: Pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMFs) may exert antimicrobial effects, which could be relevant both in medical applications and as a contributing factor in electro-disinfection processes. This study was designed to evaluate their impact on the viability of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (ATCC 27853). Experiments were performed in three independent biological replicates, each with three technical replicates per group.

pmc-13361571.title: Prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, and risk factors of pneumococcal disease among preschool children in Bushenyi District, Uganda
pmc-13361571.creator: Abdifitah Abdullahi Mohamed, Eilu Emmanuel, Chinyere Nkemjika Anyanwu, Theophilus Pius, Wesam Taher Almagharbeh, Danladi Makeri
pmc-13361571.description: BackgroundPneumococcal disease remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children in low-resource settings, with Streptococcus pneumoniae being the leading bacterial pathogen. This study sought to determine the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) patterns, and the socio-environmental risk factors associated with S. pneumoniae among hospitalized preschool children.

pmc-13392869.title: The adaptation of the gut microbiome to social environmental changes in an Asian langur
pmc-13392869.creator: Yanqiong Chen, Ying Lai, Zheng Liu, Kechu Zhang, Jingjin Zheng, Shiyi Lu, Zhonghao Huang
pmc-13392869.description: SummarySocial environments profoundly impact social animals’ gut microbiome. Understanding such effects is critical for evaluating population fitness and conservation. Employing 16S rRNA and metagenomic sequencing, we investigated the gut microbiome of the endangered white-headed langur (Trachypithecus leucocephalus) to clarify its potential adaptive strategies to social environmental changes.
